messages:
Priya: Quick sync — kicking off a small, surgical quarterly access review focused on infra svcaccts + analytics. Goal: remove stale admin entitlements, confirm owners for KMS keybindings, and capture 'owner proof' artifacts. Doing a 10% sample sweep starting tomorrow.

Priya: TL;DR plan: 1) gather evidence for each admin entitlement (owner email + attestation), 2) flag orphans, 3) run canary disable for one project, 4) prune after 48h if no evidence. Thoughts?

Noah: +1 on canary. what's the query you'll run to find candidate service accounts?

Priya: Using the rbac-audit tool first: 
```
rbac-audit --roles admin,owner --age >90d --output json --projects prod,staging
```
That gives a csv/json dump we can attach to tickets. Then cross-ref with KMS bindings: 
```
gcloud kms keys list --location=global --keyring=prod-keyring --format=json
# then check IAM bindings per key
```

Cara: Can eng-sre run the KMS binding check? I don't have perms in prod keyrings.

Devon: I can run the key binding probe — will post the delta. Also recommend we include a short evidence template so owners know what to reply with.

Priya: Evidence template (short): owner email, ticket link (if feature or infra change), CI job name or PR, and a one-line justification. We'll attach a 48h disable window notice. Example in ticket: "we will disable admin role for svcacct X at 2026-03-30T17:00Z unless owner responds"

sec-bot: Auto-check: found 12 svcaccts with admin role and last-used >120d across prod/staging. See /tmp/priv_sweep_5223.json (uploaded).

Noah: Please confirm sensitivity: are any of those tied to scheduled cron jobs? I can run last-authn lookup: 
```
acct-usage --service-accounts --since 365d --last-authn
```

Priya: Good call. We will exclude any with recent authn or active CI references. The rest become prune candidates.

eng-sre-bot: KMS check complete: keys with broad members: projects/prod/serviceAccounts/analytics-processor@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com -> roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter (last bind 2025-12-14). 3 keys flagged as admin-binding-like.

Devon: I'll open tickets for each flagged acct. Suggested labels: security:access-review, owner-request, canary-disable.

Cara: One request — please include rollback/playbook steps in each ticket (how to re-enable fast, run health checks, and who to page).

Priya: Will do. Proposed canary schedule: pick one non-critical project on Wed 10am PT, disable admin on 1 svcacct, monitor 48h. If any automated alerts or owner pushback, revert within 15 min.

Noah: I'm happy to monitor metrics and alerting. I'll add a CloudWatch/GCP metrics dashboard widget for 48h.

Priya: If everyone OK, we'll start the sweep tomorrow morning. Devon + eng-sre to run queries and open tickets. I'll prepare the owner evidence template + canned PR for rollback.

Cara: :thumbsup: Please ping #eng-oncall and #product if you think user-facing jobs could be impacted.

Priya: Will do. Also adding a quick note for KMS owners: we need a short attestation that their key binding to a svcacct is required. If not returned, we'll move to least-privileging the binding (encrypter->viewer) as part of the prune.

Devon: One operational question — for keys used by ephemeral infra (k8s secrets CSI), how aggressive shall we be? Some are used by cron rotation and don't show regular authn.

Noah: For CSI/rotation, require a short infra owner confirmation (ticket + job name). If no reply, don't prune automatically; escalate to infra lead for manual review.

Priya: Agreed. Escalation path: infra lead -> platform PM -> sec-eng. We'll add that to each ticket.

eng-sre-bot: Action items created: #SRV-4581 (canary disable), #SRV-4582..#SRV-4584 (evidence collection). Links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRV-4581

Priya: Great — thanks all. Expect status updates in this thread tomorrow with the initial CSV and KMS deltas. If anyone wants to join the canary window monitoring, DM me.

Cara: Thanks — will standby.

Devon: Starting queries now, will upload outputs to the ticket.

Priya: Closing for now — continuing in-thread for updates.
